parsed.explanation: National birth-sex public-restroom rule is a traveler-facing universal exposure: it can force document checks, denial of identity-matching facilities, and confrontation, with no documented effective remedy specific to the rule. Trans identity is not criminalised, same-sex conduct is lawful, and there is no documented organized targeting, custody, border or care restriction, which keeps it out of severe-risk territory. Absence of gender-identity hate-crime/anti-discrimination coverage, public-institution hostility and vague child-integrity/censorship language are climate aggravators. Positive signals—a delayed police-torture conviction, an anti-equality decree ruled unconstitutional, pride activity and youth acceptance—show institutional checks but do not offset the enforced restroom restriction. Violence magnitude is unresolved, and open questions are not penalized as exposures. Net: elevated risk, around the lower-middle of that band.
